about: Expected verdicts of the example packets of APRS12c under the reading in docs/legacy/. Examples are named by PDF page and the first 8 hex digits of the BLAKE3 digest of their extracted bytes (qua-legacy-examples extract); the bytes are not stored here. Derived from the documents in docs/legacy/ alone, without running the tokenizer, so that the list can check it.

The extraction lost the script-l symbol code and the line-area descriptor with its 100-mile corridor in braces, which should follow the longitude directly. The restored packet would still get the same verdict.

examples.note: Positionless report: the MDHM stamp at 1-8 is in range, and the leading c, s, g and t elements are at 9, 13, 17 and 21. Next come r, p, P, h and b; the 5-digit pressure is at 40-45. The 4-byte tail at offset 46 begins with a letter. Its last three bytes are the listed unit RSW, so it splits as software code w (added by the erratum) plus that unit. A tail of 3 or 4 bytes that starts with a letter always gets the ambiguous finding against wx.sw. The 'w' is not followed by a digit, so amb.wx.letters gives nothing.
examples.doubt: Rule ID of the discouraged finding: 'dti' or possibly wx.pl.

examples.note: The dots here are unknown fill, not an ellipsis. The c, s, g and t values are each three dots, which is allowed, at offsets 9, 13, 17 and 21, and the rain-since-midnight element is at 25. The 3-byte tail at offset 29 is not a listed unit, nor a listed unit after its first byte, and its first byte is not a listed software code. It is read as a 3-byte wx.unit and gets the two-way-split ambiguous finding against wx.sw. Its first letter is undefined but is not followed by a digit, so amb.wx.letters gives nothing.
examples.doubt: Rule ID of the discouraged finding: 'dti' or possibly wx.pl.

examples.note: Complete weather report (symbol '_' at 19): wind at 20, elements g,t,r,p,P,h,b from 27 to 55, 4-byte tail at 56 split as software 'w' plus listed unit RSW; a 3-4 byte tail starting with a letter always gives the tail ambiguity.

Same report with pressure unknown; the PDF text layer itself has dot, SP, three dots, so the pressure value mixes fill kinds, 'b' starts no element, the data ends at 50 and the 10 remaining bytes are no valid tail: residue named after wx.unit with syntax.
examples.doubt: The gap is an erratum of the document (err.wx.unknown-example), not of the extraction; the erratum says the reading takes it as five dots, which would give conform-ambiguous with 'ambiguous wx.sw @56'. Given here on the bytes as printed.

examples.note: Extraction cut the compressed weather example at the escaped underscore; the printed field continues with the '_' symbol, cs, T and the weather data and tail. As extracted the block stops after the symbol code '>' at 10, so cs and T are missing from offset 11. The finding is on cmp.block under the short-block rule of 02 section 6.2, written after this entry was first derived.
examples.doubt: Rule id of a missing-byte finding inside the 13-byte block (cmp.cs vs cmp.block) is not stated explicitly; placed at the first missing byte.

examples.note: Timestamped complete weather report; negative temperature form at 38 is valid; tail of 4 bytes at 63 gets the tail ambiguity.

A weather object (byte 0 carries wx.obj). Wind 220/004 is at 37-43 and gust g005 at 44-47. The pressure element at 48 has only four digits, so it does not start an element, and the data ends there. The 5-byte tail splits into software code 'b' (not in the software list, so unstated) and unit 0990. Reading (b) of amb.wx.width would take the short pressure as the element and leave an empty tail with no finding of its own, so the tail gets an ambiguous finding at its first byte, against wx.baro. The missing temperature gives no finding in a complete report.
examples.doubt: err.wx.object-baro describes only the tail split and does not mention the ambiguous finding. I took that finding from the second condition of amb.wx.width.

examples.note: Extraction cut the timestamped compressed weather example before its '_' symbol code; the printed field continues with symbol, cs, T, weather data and tail. The finding is on cmp.block under the short-block rule of 02 section 6.2, written after this entry was first derived.
examples.doubt: Rule id for the missing byte (cmp.code vs cmp.block) not stated explicitly.

Telemetry report: the sequence '#' plus three digits and a comma is at 1-5, five three-digit analog values are at 6-25, and the eight bits are at 26-33. There is no comment.

The sequence is MIC with no comma (offsets 1-4), and the analog values start at offset 5. Reading (c) would take the first value into the sequence and then need the comment to supply a fifth value and the bits. The comment is empty, so (c) fails and no ambiguous finding is given at offset 5.
Diagram cell for the telemetry sequence number; xxx is a placeholder.
The sequence is 3 digits. All five analog values are decimals and one is negative, so each is the relaxed number and gives unstated. The digital value is at 31-38, with no comment.
examples.doubt: The reading does not state where the unstated finding goes; I put it at the first byte of each value. The relaxed grammar puts its optional '-' before 'digits'; I read the sign as applying to the decimal forms as well, as err.tlm.analog implies for the negative value. Otherwise the fifth value would give syntax.

If the unstated were inherited, each non-three-digit coefficient would carry one (no verdict effect).
